import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from sklearn.linear_model import LinearRegression
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('/data/worldbank_education_gdp.csv')

# Identify the rows with the relevant series names
labor_force_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'Labor force participation rate, total (percentage of total population ages 15+) (modeled ILO estimate)'].index[0]
primary_enrollment_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'School enrollment, primary (percentage gross)'].index[0]
secondary_enrollment_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'School enrollment, secondary (percentage gross)'].index[0]
export_growth_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'Exports of goods and services (annual percentage growth)'].index[0]

# Extract the relevant data
labor_force_data = df.iloc[labor_force_row, 4:]
primary_enrollment_data = df.iloc[primary_enrollment_row, 4:]
secondary_enrollment_data = df.iloc[secondary_enrollment_row, 4:]
export_growth_data = df.iloc[export_growth_row, 4:]

# Combine the data into a single DataFrame
data = pd.DataFrame({
    'Labor Force Participation': labor_force_data.values,
    'Primary Enrollment': primary_enrollment_data.values,
    'Secondary Enrollment': secondary_enrollment_data.values,
    'Export Growth': export_growth_data.values
})

# Impute missing values with the mean of the respective columns
imputer = SimpleImputer(strategy='mean')
data_imputed = pd.DataFrame(imputer.fit_transform(data), columns=data.columns)

# Perform linear regression
X = data_imputed[['Labor Force Participation', 'Primary Enrollment', 'Secondary Enrollment']]
y = data_imputed['Export Growth']

model = LinearRegression()
model.fit(X, y)

coefficients = model.coef_
intercept = model.intercept_

coefficients, intercept
